clue.text: Excellent, child by ring showing off a martial art

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI
a kid is a child
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A youngster in the ring shows off moves from a Japanese fighting discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'showing off' are link words joining the pieces to the definition; A1 (first-rate) is read as the letters AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Aikido is a Japanese defensive combat discipline built on throws and joint locks.

clue.text: What can make prelims simpler?

parts.note: the letters of prelims, rearranged, spell simpler: the device that turns one word into the other is being described

explanation.definitionFit: Rearranging the letters of one word to form another is exactly this wordplay device.

clue.text: Bite dog in film!

parts.note: a drink with bite has a kick, a sharp strong taste
a boxer is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A dog bites someone during a movie, worthy of an exclamation mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; the film is the 1989 martial-arts movie starring Jean-Claude Van Damme.
explanation.definitionFit: Kickboxer is the title of a 1989 action movie.

clue.text: Give university teacher a note

parts.note: a don is a lecturer at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge
taken as written
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A request to hand a lecturer a short written message.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to give something, typically to a cause or charity.

clue.text: Youngest son's overcoat

explanation.surface: The baby of the family's heavy coat.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Benjamin is Jacob's youngest son, hence any youngest child; a benjamin was also a nineteenth-century man's overcoat.

clue.text: They may be seen inside creel, slithering

definitions.text: They may be seen inside creel, slithering

indicators.note: the word inside tells us the letters sit within the run of words creel slithering

explanation.surface: Wriggling fish in an angler's basket.
explanation.walkthrough: A creel is a fisherman's wicker basket; the answer is tucked across the end of creel and the start of slithering, and the whole clue describes it too.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakelike fish slither about in a fisherman's basket when caught.

clue.text: Spring fashion garment

parts.note: to spring is to jump
to fashion or suit something is to adapt it to fit

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing in this season's new collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring fashion' reads as a season's styles, but Spring is the verb leap and fashion the verb adapt.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumpsuit is a one-piece item of clothing covering the body and legs.

clue.text: Copper, and others, after leader of mob?

indicators.note: after places the and-others piece behind the first letter of mob
the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from mob

parts.note: et al is Latin shorthand for and others

explanation.surface: A policeman and his colleagues chasing a gang boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' reads as a police officer, but it is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is an example of a metal, a conductive element.

clue.text: Budding early in North America with pleasant smell

parts.note: a scent is a pleasant smell

explanation.surface: Spring flowers opening early across the US, with a lovely fragrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nascent is just beginning to develop, coming into being.

clue.text: Understood by few, British composer seen round about

indicators.note: the composer is seen round, wrapped about, the short word for about

parts.note: Thomas Arne was an English composer, writer of Rule, Britannia!
ca, from circa, means about

explanation.surface: A British composer whose music only a few appreciate.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcane knowledge is secret or esoteric, grasped only by the initiated.

clue.text: Climbing plant of variable climates

indicators.note: variable means changeable, so the letters of climates are rearranged

explanation.surface: A creeper that grows in a range of different weather zones.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a flowering vine that scrambles up walls and trellises.

clue.text: Clothes torn keeping goal

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: rent is an old past form of rend, meaning torn
an aim is a goal

explanation.surface: Garments ripped while the wearer guards the net.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an archaic word for clothing or dress.

clue.text: True about Aunt Sally making a denial

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for true goes round the target

parts.note: real means true
an Aunt Sally, from a British fairground game of throwing at a dummy, is a target of criticism, a butt

explanation.surface: Someone insists a fairground target story is accurate, denying the accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aunt Sally is a British pub and fairground game of hurling sticks at a figure; figuratively, an easy target.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a refutation, a contradiction of a claim.

clue.text: Irish princess died in one, alone

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for died within the other pieces

parts.note: sole means alone, single

explanation.surface: A princess from Ireland died by herself.
explanation.walkthrough: The princess is the Irish heroine of the Tristan legend and Wagner's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend Isolde is the Irish king's daughter who loves Tristan.

clue.text: Ring one about fashionable cocktail

indicators.note: about means around, so the ring and one go about the fashionable piece

parts.note: to ring is to bell, sound a bell
I is the Roman numeral one
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Phone someone about a trendy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bellini is a Venetian drink of prosecco and peach purée.

clue.text: Ms Zetterling keeping by a long skirt

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the actress's name holds the multiplication sign

parts.note: Mai Zetterling was a Swedish actress and director
x is the times sign, read as by in dimensions such as two by four

explanation.surface: A Swedish actress holding onto a lengthy garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' gives X because measurements are spoken as 'three by four' and written 3 x 4.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxi is a skirt or dress reaching the ankles.

clue.text: Paraphernalia, not a hindrance

indicators.note: not means the letter a in the clue is left out

parts.note: impedimenta is baggage or equipment, paraphernalia

explanation.surface: Insisting that a heap of gear is not an obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: An impediment is an obstacle or obstruction.

clue.text: Ivy, always pale and sickly-looking?

parts.note: ever means always
someone green looks pale and nauseous

explanation.surface: A person named Ivy perpetually looks ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ivy' looks like a woman's name, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is an example of a plant that keeps its leaves all year.

clue.text: Sharper southern wind over the French river

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the earlier pieces sit above the later ones

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A colder breeze from the south blows across a river in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharper' looks like a comparative adjective, but it is a noun: a cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharper is a cheat or con man, especially at cards.

clue.text: Shellfish plant

explanation.definitionFit: A periwinkle is both an edible sea snail and a trailing plant with blue flowers.

clue.text: Large company securing Italian wine with credit cards

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the company holds the wine inside

parts.note: PLC, public limited company, is a large British company
Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont

explanation.surface: A big firm stocking up on Italian wine and paying by card.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic is slang for bank cards, used in paying.

clue.text: Son in plane makes a joke

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for son inside the aircraft

parts.note: a jet is a plane

explanation.surface: A boy on an aircraft clowns around.
explanation.definitionFit: To jest is to joke, say something in fun.

clue.text: Whirlwind broke up a party

parts.note: something broken up is torn apart
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A tempest ruined an outdoor celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating storm column.

clue.text: Spite shown by married woman

parts.note: Alice is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A wife displaying resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the desire to harm, ill will.

clue.text: Representative capturing second in triathlon gets silver

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so the representative takes in the picked letter

parts.note: an agent is a representative

indicators.note: the second letter in triathlon is picked

explanation.surface: An athlete's agent claims a runner-up medal in a three-sport race.
explanation.walkthrough: Argent is the heraldic term for silver.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry argent is the tincture of silver or white.

clue.text: Good and ready to complain

parts.note: fruit that is ripe is ready to eat

explanation.surface: Someone well prepared to voice a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: To gripe is to grumble or moan.

clue.text: Aim to provoke menace

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
to anger is to provoke

explanation.surface: An intention to stir up trouble and threaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger is to put at risk, threaten.

clue.text: Nickname for Louise, something that's remarkable

explanation.surface: A pet name for a girl who is something special.
explanation.definitionFit: Lulu is a familiar short form of Louise, and a lulu is informal for an outstanding person or thing.

clue.text: Manage after hearing test

indicators.note: after puts the word for manage behind the word for hearing

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing
to run something is to manage it

explanation.surface: A manager going for a hearing test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' is not a sound signal here: a court hearing is a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run is a rehearsal or practice test of something.

clue.text: The last word I caught back in picture palace

indicators.note: back means the run of pieces is read in reverse order

parts.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer, the last word
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Getting the final say in a picture house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AMENIC round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Picture palace is an old-fashioned term for a movie theatre.

clue.text: Awfully cruel act seen in black and white

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters of cruel act are rearranged

explanation.surface: A terribly cruel deed witnessed in a monochrome photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is a link word; black and white here means unambiguous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clear-cut is definite and unambiguous, with no shades of grey.

clue.text: Slowly circling a type of shed

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the musical term surrounds the letter a

parts.note: lento is the musical direction for slowly

explanation.surface: Walking slowly round a garden outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a shed built against a wall with a single sloping roof.
